nodes.name: InNNi₃ synthesis
nodes.procedure: Stoichiometric amounts of In₂O₃ and NiO powders were first dispersed in ethanol and milled at 400 rpm for 1 h in a planetary mill (Fritsch, Pulverisette 6). After being dried, this homogeneous precursor mixture was then annealed at 500 °C for 5 h under NH₃ atmosphere to obtain InNNi₃ powders.

nodes.name: Ni₃N synthesis
nodes.procedure: The nitride Ni₃N was synthesized by the identical procedure as InNNi₃, with the exception of the distinction of raw materials and calcinations conditions (i.e., 370 °C for 10 h).
nodes.source_text: The nitride Ni₃N was synthesized by the identical procedure as InNNi₃, with the exception of the distinction of raw materials and calcinations conditions (i.e., 370 °C for 10 h).

nodes.name: EO-InNNi₃ electrochemical oxidation
nodes.procedure: EO-InNNi₃ was prepared from an electrochemical oxidation treatment of InNNi₃ via 200 consecutive cycle voltammetry scans at anodic potentials (i.e., 0.2-0.8 V vs Hg/HgO) in 1 M KOH solution.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of EO-InNNi₃ and EO-Ni₃N: EO-InNNi₃ was prepared from an electrochemical oxidation treatment of InNNi₃ via 200 consecutive cycle voltammetry scans at anodic potentials (i.e., 0.2-0.8 V vs Hg/HgO) in 1 m KOH solution.

nodes.name: EO-Ni₃N electrochemical oxidation
nodes.procedure: The EO-Ni₃N was synthesized from Ni₃N according to the same method as that of the EO-InNNi₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction peaks match cubic InNNi₃ phase (Pm-3m) with lattice parameter a = b = c = 3.8634(1) Å and no detectable impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b displays the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of as-prepared InNNi₃. All the diffraction peaks match well with the cubic InNNi₃ phase (Pm·3m) without detectable impurities.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with observed, calculated, background, and difference traces

nodes.characterization_summary: Interplanar spacings of 0.39 nm and 0.27 nm correspond to (001) and (110) facets of cubic InNNi₃, confirmed by FFT pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Figure 2c), the observed interplanar spacing of 0.39 and 0.27 nm correspond to the (001) and (110) facets of cubic phase InNNi₃, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS In 3d and Ni 2p spectra show In⁰/In³⁺ and Ni⁰/Ni²⁺ states with enhanced Ni⁰/Ni²⁺ ratio vs Ni₃N; N 1s peaks at 397.5 eV (Ni/In-N) and 399.3 eV (N-H) confirm metal-nitride bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 2f,g, the In and Ni elements exist in form of In⁰/In³⁺ and Ni⁰/Ni²⁺... the Ni⁰/Ni²⁺ intensity ratio of InNNi₃ exhibits evident enhancement... two featured peaks... at 397.5 and 399.3 eV in the N 1s spectrum...

properties.description: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy spectrum for Ni 2p region

nodes.characterization_summary: Small Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area observed, indicating bulk nature of InNNi₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Submicron-sized particles (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and small Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area (Figure S3, Supporting Information) were observed for InNNi₃...

nodes.characterization_summary: Amorphous InNi(oxy)hydroxide shell (no lattice fringes, halo in FFT); core shows 0.27 nm and 0.39 nm spacings for (110) and (001) planes of InNNi₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The shell is characteristic of an amorphous phase because no clear lattice fringes were seen in the HRTEM image... Conversely, two lattice spacings of 0.27 and 0.39 nm corresponding to the (110) and (001) planes of InNNi₃...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pronounced O signal in marginal region with ≈40 nm thick amorphous InNi(oxy)hydroxide layer on InNNi₃ surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EO-InNNi₃ exhibits a pronounced O signals in the marginal region in the EDS line-scan (Figure 3e)... suggesting the generation of a thin amorphous InNi (oxy)hydroxide layer (≈40 nm)...

properties.description: Energy Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan counts vs distance

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows complete disappearance of N 1s signal and In⁰/Ni⁰ peaks in EO-InNNi₃; new hydroxide peak at ≈531.3 eV in O 1s confirms amorphous InNi(oxy)hydroxide shell formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the formation of the surficial (oxo)hydroxide was also confirmed by the XPS analysis, which is reflected by the complete disappearance of N 1s signal as well as the peaks of In⁰ and Ni⁰... and the appearance of a new hydroxide peak (≈531.3 eV) in the O 1s spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values of 1.73 mF cm⁻² for EO-InNNi₃ (higher than 0.82 mF cm⁻² for InNNi₃), indicating more exposed active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value (1.73 mF cm⁻²) of EO-InNNi₃ is higher than that (0.82 mF cm⁻²) of InNNi₃ (Figure S11, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows β-NiOOH formation at lower potential (1.5 V) for EO-InNNi₃ vs InNNi₃ (1.6 V) with higher I₄₇₇/I₅₇₇ ratio indicating more active β-NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Note that the potential-dependent structure transformation is realized at a lower potential of 1.5 V for the EO-InNNi₃ relative to that (1.6 V) for pristine InNNi₃... Higher I₄₇₇/I₅₇₇ peak intensity ratio means more generation of β-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows homogeneous spatial distribution of In, N, and Ni elements over InNNi₃ material.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy disperse spectrum (EDS) elemental mapping demonstrates the homogeneous spatial distribution of In, N, and Ni elements over the InNNi₃ material
